header.sector: Hyperscaler / cloud AI capital expenditure and the companies spending it
header.title: Hyperscaler capex may face financing, power and model-competition limits

s01_bottom_line.text: The speaker frames three market concerns pressuring the AI capex trade: a cost-of-capital/financing squeeze on levered AI players and neoclouds, an inability to energize 20-40/50GW of power next year, and more competition at the model layer, driving investor de-risking. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
The article says the market is de-risking the AI/AI-capex trade and watching hyperscaler monetization and FCF breakeven closely as the key swing factor for credit and risk.

If any of these constraints bind, hyperscaler and AI-infrastructure capex and the related suppliers' volumes could fall short of the ~$1.1tn market expectation; the article does not quantify the earnings hit.

items.text: The range of deliverable power for next year is roughly 20 to 40-50 gigawatts. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Market expectation for hyperscaler capex is around $1.1 trillion for next year. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Last week saw the biggest selling of tech ever recorded in the GS prime book.
Cost of capital has spilled over broadly, seen in CCC spreads, European sovereign spreads and the more levered parts of the AI trade/neoclouds.
Investors were very concentrated within AI, semis and hyperscalers.
There is more competition at the AI model layer.
